title: RC-11 head-of-line blocking: a snipe buy holds the wallet nonce lock through its private attempts until its own 60 s swap deadline makes the relay refuse the next one (about 105 s and 2 bundles at default settings when the bundle does not land), so an anti-rug emergency sell of another position cannot start, times out after 60 s and is left queued, to run only when the buy lets go

evidence.note: submitBuyTx = withNonceLock(wallet, () => sendTxWithRetry(txBuilder, ctx)): one lock hold covers the whole escalation

buys pass no explicit retry budget, so retries = 3: a budget of attempts 0..3 = 4 private submissions; on a realistic relay the swap deadline ends a non-landing snipe after 2 of them (2026-11-12 measurement below)

each attempt: re-fetch nonce, submit, then (not natively confirmed) reconcileInclusion over confirmWindowMs; the loop only stops early when the clamped fee hits the ceiling or the affordability bound (:551-553, :606)
default confirm window 45000 ms, poll 4000 ms

escalated priority fee = step x (attempt+1) = 1, 2, 3, 4 gwei by default, far below the 25 gwei buy ceiling (:69), so at calm gas the ceiling never ends the loop early (on a realistic relay the swap deadline ends it after the 1 and 2 gwei attempts)

per attempt on ETH: library sendBundle, a raw fanout call per target block (default 3), then bundle.wait() until the first target block passes (about 12 s), then getBundleStatsV2 (:343-366), all inside the lock
on BSC every submit returns nativeConfirmed false, so every attempt spends the full confirm window under the lock
an anti-rug exit of another token first needs the same wallet lock for its approval, then again for the private sell (:909 via :782-789)
withTimeout frees the anti-rug caller at 60 s and records success=false; the executeFullSell it started keeps running and stays queued on the nonce lock
strict FIFO: no priority lane, no abort, no way for an emergency op to jump the queue

the snipe swap deadline is now + 60 s, set once when the swap is built; sendTxWithRetry calls the builder once (src/utils/txManager.ts:113) and every attempt re-signs the same calldata (src/utils/mevStrategies/flashbots.ts:192), so the escalation reaches attempts whose deadline has passed

evidence.ref: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project realpath test/realpath/triage/AUD-TX-003.test.ts (Node 22.16.0, 2026-11-12; realistic reverts are the simulated chain default since 780d67d; test re-triaged in 354e2fc)
evidence.note: claim antirug-exit-queued-behind-buy still records {emergencySellStartedWithinBudget:false}. Fake-clock timings: B's first bundle 220 ms after its launch; anti-rug dispatch for A 8 020 ms after B's first submission; B's attempt 0 not-landed at dispatch + 44 230; antirug.exit.bounded-abort exactly dispatch + 60 000; B's attempt 1 (sent inside its deadline) not-landed at dispatch + 96 520; attempt 2's eth_callBundle refused (flashbots.simulate.revert attempt 2) and buy.snipe.fail-clean at dispatch + 96 540, reason 'Flashbots simulate: tx would revert (execution reverted)'; A's abandoned exit first sends at dispatch + 96 610, then sells the remains. B held the lock about 104.6 s with 2 bundles at one nonce. Asserted after the marker: 2 B bundles, the refused attempt-2 simulation with the decoded swap deadline already past, fail-clean 90 to 120 s after B's first submission, A's first send at or after the fail-clean

sibling_sites_checked: All long holders of the wallet lock: submitBuyTx (bot.ts:267, snipe, 4 attempts), the deliberate private leg (bot.ts:558, DELIBERATE_BUY_PRIVATE_ATTEMPTS default 2), routine private sells (exitEngine.ts:788, MEV_SELL_FALLBACK_ATTEMPTS default 2) and partial sells (:1531, default 4 attempts), plus every wait() holder in AUD-TX-002. The sell-behind-sell case (a routine exit of token A delaying the anti-rug exit of token B) is already AUD-EXIT-014; this entry is the buy-escalation case RC-11 names and the lock policy itself. That a refused or timed-out anti-rug escape is not retried by the detector is AUD-ANTIRUG-004.
severity_rationale: S1, equal to the research suggestion. Condition: a rug on one held position while a snipe for another token is escalating privately on the same wallet, which is ordinary operation for a sniping bot (snipes that do not land were the Phase 21.3 calm-gas problem). Default timing on ETH, measured on the real path with a simulated relay that refuses an expired swap as a real one does (Phase 23 code-review fix run, WR-01; wording corrected 2026-11-12 by operator ruling, process note PN-002): each private attempt takes about 52 s (the first target block, the stats call and the 45 s confirm window) and the swap deadline is fixed once when the swap is built (src/bot.ts:1043, now + 60 s), so the snipe sends 2 bundles and the relay refuses the third attempt's simulation as UniswapV2Router: EXPIRED; the snipe holds the lock about 105 s and then fails clean. An anti-rug exit dispatched 8.0 s into that escalation still cannot start and gives up at exactly 60 000 ms, the detector does not retry it (AUD-ANTIRUG-004), and the abandoned sell first sends at dispatch + 96.6 s, at whatever price is left. The earlier code-read figure (4 attempts, about 4 minutes) assumed a relay that accepts an expired swap. Any rug dispatched in roughly the first 45 s of a non-landing snipe still loses its whole 60 s budget, so the grade stands. The BSC timing (bloXroute: every attempt waits the full 45 s confirm window) is a code read and was not re-measured.
recommendation: Phase 24 (card OD-17, head-of-line part): decide how an emergency exit gets the wallet. Options on the card: a priority lane in the nonce authority for anti-rug exits, an abortable buy escalation that yields the lock between attempts, or releasing the lock between attempts with the nonce re-checked. Whatever is chosen, an abandoned (timed-out) exit must be cancelled or reconciled, not left queued to run minutes later. Prove the timing in Phase 23 with a held position, a non-landing private buy and a simulated rug on a local fork. Nothing is changed in Phase 22.

traces.scenario: A rug on held token A while a snipe of token B escalates privately on ETH (defaults; times from B's first submission, measured on the real path with a relay that refuses an expired swap, 2026-11-12)
steps: t=0: the pair handler for B builds the swap with deadline now + 60 s (bot.ts:1043) and calls submitBuyTx; withNonceLock(wallet) starts the escalation (bot.ts:267)

attempt 0 (1 gwei): nonce fetch, sign, simulate (accepted), sendBundle, 3 raw fanout calls, bundle.wait() until head+1 passes, getBundleStatsV2, then reconcileInclusion polls for 45 s (reconciliation.ts:576-583) and finds not-landed at about t=52 s

t=8 s: the anti-rug detector fires for A; exitTrigger calls executeFullSell under withTimeout(60000) (exitTrigger.ts:265-269); executeFullSell takes A's per-token sell lock, then queues for the wallet lock to approve (exitEngine.ts:871/874)
attempt 1 (2 gwei): the same calldata is simulated just inside the deadline, sent, and found not-landed at about t=105 s
t=68 s: withTimeout fires exactly 60 000 ms after the dispatch; anti-rug logs bounded-abort and returns false; the detector does not re-fire for that rug (AUD-ANTIRUG-004)

t=~105 s: the relay refuses attempt 2's simulation (UniswapV2Router: EXPIRED, the deadline fixed at build has passed), the snipe fails clean and lets the lock go; the queued executeFullSell for A now approves (first send at dispatch + 96.6 s) and sells, with the balance it read before queuing and at whatever price is left; meanwhile every other exit of A was refused by the sell lock (AUD-EXIT-014)
traces.outcome: Token A is held through the rug with no working exit for about 97 s after the anti-rug dispatch (longer for a rug earlier in the escalation), and then sold late. Capital: most of A's value can be gone (STRAND turning into LOSS). The operator sees an anti-rug watchdog-abort alert that says the position "will retry", which it does not do by itself.

sub_claims.claim: A non-landing snipe holds the wallet lock through its private attempts until its own swap deadline ends the escalation: about 105 s on ETH at default settings (2 bundles, then the relay refuses the third attempt's simulation as UniswapV2Router: EXPIRED), measured on the real path on 2026-11-12; the earlier code-read figure of about 4 minutes and 4 attempts assumed a relay that accepts an expired swap
evidence: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project realpath test/realpath/triage/AUD-TX-003.test.ts (Node 22.16.0, 2026-11-12, realistic reverts by default)

sub_claims.claim: The nonce authority has no priority or abort path for an emergency exit
A timed-out anti-rug exit stays queued and runs later instead of being cancelled
evidence: node tx-lock-repro.js <snapshot> (Node 22.16.0, scratch folder outside the repo; loads the base-SHA snapshot of src/utils/nonceAuthority.ts via typescript.transpileModule plus ethers@6.16.0 TransactionResponse on a fake provider; no src/ import, no SQLite, no .env, no network)

triage.note: Reproduced on the real path with the order forced (plan 23-09, AC-12; re-triaged on the realistic chain in the Phase 23 code-review fix run, WR-01, wording corrected by operator ruling 2026-11-12, PN-002): one ETH wallet holds position A (uniswap-v2, anti-rug live, bought and armed); 31 s later the bot snipes token B on sushiswap-v2 and B's bundles are never included, so submitBuyTx holds the wallet lock; 8.0 s after B's first submission a real 95 percent liquidity pull of A is evaluated unsafe and the anti-rug exit is dispatched; its approval queues on the wallet lock, nothing of A is sent, and antirug.exit.bounded-abort is logged exactly 60000 fake ms after antirug.exit.dispatch on the timeline (claim antirug-exit-queued-behind-buy). B sends 2 bundles at one nonce; the relay refuses its third attempt's simulation because the swap deadline fixed at build (now + 60 s, decoded from B's signed bundle) has passed, so B fails clean about 105 s after its first submission ('Flashbots simulate: tx would revert (execution reverted)'); only then does A's abandoned exit send its approval (dispatch + 96.6 s) and sell the remains. An anti-rug approval that skips the queue reads looks fixed; a priority lane for the anti-rug private sell alone (the approval still queues) records the bug unchanged. The pull's extra dispatches refused by the held sell lock are AUD-ANTIRUG-003 / AUD-EXIT-014 territory and are not counted here.
